headline: Every viral 2025-26 "small-account day-trading algo" claim family is dominated by survivorship bias, hidden leverage, prop-firm fee economics, or backtest overfitting (base rates: 74-97% of retail day traders lose; +40%/month = 5,568%/yr, 84x Medallion's gross), yet five narrow techniques — relative-volume "in play" gating, first-15-min entry avoidance, VWAP-relative entry pricing, first-half-hour intraday-momentum tilt, and volatility-scaled sizing — have real published evidence and port cleanly to an hourly LLM-decides + deterministic-risk-gate Alpaca bot.
evidence: FAMILY 1 — ORB bots ('opening range breakout', the dominant 2025-26 YouTube/fintwit algo claim, typically $1k-25k accounts claiming 100-400%/yr): the real academic result (Zarattini, Barbon & Aziz 2024, SSRN 4729284) is 41.6% annualized IRR / Sharpe 2.81 (2016-2023, 7,000+ stocks) — but the plain 5-min ORB was WEAK; nearly all edge came from restricting to the top-20 stocks by opening relative volume ('stocks in play'), and headline returns assume frictionless fills; QuantConnect replication got Sharpe 2.4. VERDICT: genuine regime-conditional edge, but influencers copy the breakout pattern and drop the relative-volume filter that did the work. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4729284 ; https://www.quantconnect.com/research/18444/opening-range-breakout-for-stocks-in-play/

FAMILY 1 decay/costs: retail ORB variants show negative long-run expectancy — a TradingView ORB+VWAP-filter backtest won 39.09% of 243 trades in 2025 but returned -99.26% over 2010-2026; ORB option-selling equity curves went choppy after Jan 2024 and never recovered from the mid-2024 drawdown; the widely-shared 9,350% ORB variant came from a parameter search with zero slippage assumed. https://danfin.net/opening-range-breakout-research ; https://www.tradingview.com/script/wLSGHPUe-ORB-Breakout-Strategy-with-VWAP-and-Volume-Filters/

BASE RATES (applies to all families): Chague & De-Losso (Brazil, ~20,000 persistent day traders over 300+ sessions) found 97% lost money; Barber-Lee-Liu-Odean-Zhang (Taiwan, 3.7B transactions 1992-2006) found <1% of day traders reliably profitable after costs, average -23.9 bps/day, aggregate negative in 14 of 15 years — so any social-media sample of 'winning' small accounts is drawn from the 1-3% tail plus fabrications. https://faculty.haas.berkeley.edu/odean/papers/Day%20Traders/Day%20Trade%20040330.pdf ; https://www.newtrading.io/is-day-trading-profitable/

FAMILY 2 — 0DTE options (buying lottery calls on TikTok, 'theta gang' selling on YouTube; typical capital $2k-50k): University of Münster data shows retail has lost ~$358k/DAY (~$90M/yr) on 0DTE since May 2022; long positions lose on average while SHORT positions are profitable even after fees (Verdad: 0DTE systematically overpriced) — but short-gamma profit streams carry unrealized tail risk (one gap can erase years). VERDICT: selling side has modest documented edge; buying side is pure engagement bait. https://medium.com/@submartingaleoptions/retail-traders-lose-350k-daily-on-zero-days-to-expiry-0dte-options-please-read-this-if-you-25d46bdd1bfb ; https://verdadcap.com/archive/zero-day-options

FAMILY 3 — prop-firm ORB+ATR strategies ('I passed a $200k FTMO/Topstep challenge with this bot'; capital = $100-600 challenge fee, NOT the advertised account): FPFX Technologies' 300,000-account dataset shows ~14% pass evaluations, only ~7% of challenge buyers EVER receive a payout, and 1-3% stay funded past 6 months; consistency rules (max 15%/day profit contribution, first payouts capped at 6% of balance) cap even winners. The 'returns' quoted are on the fee, on simulated money — an accounting trick, and the firms' real business is challenge-fee revenue. VERDICT: engagement bait / fee funnel. https://www.quantvps.com/blog/prop-firm-statistics-2025 ; https://funderpro.com/blog/prop-trading-pass-rates-in-2025-what-the-data-really-shows/

FAMILY 4 — crypto grid & martingale bots (Pionex/XT/3Commas marketing, 'passive 1-3%/day', typical $500-10k): grids lose whenever price exits the range or volatility < fees+funding per round trip; martingale is mathematically negative-expectancy with finite capital — position size grows exponentially through a losing streak until ruin, so equity curves look smooth right up to the blow-up. VERDICT: negative expectancy with hidden risk-of-ruin; the smooth track records shown are pre-blow-up selections. https://www.mql5.com/en/blogs/post/771466 ; https://wundertrading.com/journal/en/learn/article/understanding-and-optimizing-futures-trading-with-martingale

FAMILY 5 — RL/transformer price predictors and FAMILY 6 — LLM-ensemble stock pickers ('my GPT agent returned 500%'): StockBench (arXiv 2510.02209, contamination-free Mar-Jun 2025 window, GPT-5/Claude-4/Qwen3/Kimi-K2) found most LLM agents FAIL to beat buy-and-hold; earlier 'successful' agents collapsed under strict temporal splits because models had ingested future financial data in training; RL papers require explicit probability-of-backtest-overfitting tests (arXiv 2209.05559) — no credible published live-money outperformance exists for either family. VERDICT: near-total backtest artifact; directly cautionary for any LLM-decides bot. https://stockbench.github.io/ ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.05559

FAMILY 7 — copy-trading bots (eToro/Telegram signal mirroring, $200-5k accounts): eToro's own regulatory disclosure says ~52-61% of retail CFD accounts lose money; FCA warns copy trading gives leveraged-CFD exposure users don't understand; experimental evidence shows merely viewing top-performer leaderboards increases follower risk-taking. Leaderboards are the survivorship-bias machine itself. VERDICT: negative expectancy for followers. https://www.wallstreetzen.com/blog/etoro-copy-trading-review/ ; https://tradersunion.com/interesting-articles/copy-trading-smart-investing-or-hidden-risk-tu-research/

WHY +40%/MONTH ON $5K ISN'T COMPARABLE TO A $1M BOOK: (a) arithmetic — 1.4^12 = 5,568%/yr and 1.4^60 = 5.86e8x ($10k -> $5.9 TRILLION in 5 years); Medallion, the best audited fund in history, did 66%/yr GROSS (39% net) and closed to outsiders in 1993 — sustained claims above it are self-falsifying; (b) concentration — a $5k account can put 50-100% into one 4x-margined small-cap or a single 0DTE contract, a diversified $1M book structurally cannot without single-name capacity/liquidity impact; (c) percent-vs-dollar framing — '+40%' on $5k is $2k, less than one day's normal P&L noise on $1M; (d) unrealized tail — the martingale/short-gamma months compound until the one month that returns -100%; screenshots are sampled before that month. https://www.quantifiedstrategies.com/medallion-fund-returns/

TRANSFERABLE #1 (evidence grade A) — intraday momentum overlay: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou, Journal of Financial Economics 2018 — SPY first half-hour return predicts last half-hour return, R²=1.6% (rivaling monthly-frequency predictors), stronger on volatile/high-volume/macro-news days, replicated on 10+ ETFs and APAC markets. Bot change: in afternoon decision cycles (13:00-16:00 ET), add the day's 9:30-10:00 index return sign as a directional tilt feature for index-option and momentum entries; never fade it late-day on high-volume days. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X18301351 ; https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2440866

TRANSFERABLE #2+#3 (grade B+) — relative-volume 'in play' gate + open-chop avoidance: the single factor carrying the ORB paper's 41.6% IRR was top-20 opening relative volume, so require RVOL >= ~1.5-2x at entry for momentum/starter names (deterministic pre-filter before the LLM sees the slate); and since the 9:30-9:45 window has the day's widest spreads, thinnest reliable liquidity, and most false breaks (U-shaped intraday volatility; 'by 9:45 the opening frenzy has largely resolved'), gate the first hourly cycle to require price confirmation beyond the 15/30-min opening range in the trade's direction instead of chasing opening prints — this also directly addresses the bot's prior $300k QQQ open-print sweep failure mode. https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4729284 ; https://bookmap.com/blog/trading-the-first-15-minutes-liquidity-patterns-at-the-open

TRANSFERABLE #4+#5 — VWAP-relative entry pricing (grade B-) and volatility-scaled sizing (grade B): QuantConnect 100-stock study found fading 2-SD VWAP bands wins 61-63% (71% at 3 SD) but fails badly on trend days, so use VWAP as an entry-price discipline (longs at/below VWAP unless RVOL-confirmed breakout; never buy >1.5-2 SD above VWAP) not as a standalone scalper; Moreira-Muir (JFE 2017, NBER w22208) show sizing inversely to recent variance raises Sharpe for equities (Harvey 2018 concurs) BUT Cederburg et al. 2020 find out-of-sample gains often vanish — so implement ATR/realized-vol-scaled position sizing as a deterministic RISK CAP in the risk gate (target constant dollar-vol per position), not as an alpha source. https://www.quantifiedstrategies.com/vwap-trading-strategy/ ; https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w22208/w22208.pdf ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X2030132X
surprises: The best-documented 0DTE edge is the OPPOSITE of the viral claim: systematic 0DTE sellers profit after fees while buyers fund the ~$90M/yr retail loss pool — but the seller edge is compensation for gap tail risk that short samples never show.

The celebrated ORB paper's returns are a stock-SELECTION effect (opening relative volume), not a breakout-pattern effect — the plain ORB that influencers actually teach was weak in the same study; the transferable asset is the RVOL filter, not the breakout.

StockBench found earlier LLM-trading 'wins' were partly training-data contamination (future information leaked via pretraining); under clean temporal splits most frontier-model agents failed to beat buy-and-hold — a direct, cited caution for this project's own LLM-decides architecture.

Prop-firm content solves to a fee business, not a trading business: of 300,000 real challenge accounts only ~7% ever received any payout and 1-3% stayed funded 6+ months, and 'consistency rules' claw back even legitimate winners.

Volatility-managed portfolios — the most-cited academic 'free lunch' — largely fail out-of-sample (Cederburg et al. 2020), so vol-scaling belongs in the deterministic risk gate as a sizing cap, not in the alpha stack.
40%/month compounds to 84x Medallion's gross 66%/yr and would turn $10k into ~$5.9 trillion in 5 years — the claim family is falsified by arithmetic before any strategy analysis is needed.
